blocks.heading: Invisible authority is expensive, and the bill arrives quietly.
blocks.body:
Nobody sends an invoice for being underestimated. The cost shows up as the deal that went to a worse firm with a better-known founder, the board seat that went to someone with a book, the hire who chose a company with a louder story.

By the time you notice the pattern, you have usually been paying it for years.
painPoints: You are compared on price because nothing else about you is legible from the outside.
Your best work is invisible to everyone who was not in the room when it happened.
Inbound opportunities arrive from people who found you by accident, not by reputation.
You are asked to speak on panels, not to give keynotes.
Your team cannot explain what makes you different, so neither can your market.

blocks.heading: Five principles that shape every engagement
blocks.subheading: If you disagree with these, we are not a fit — and I would rather you know that now than four weeks into a retainer.

principles.title: Authority is built on evidence, not exposure.
principles.description: Visibility without substance decays fast and takes your reputation with it. We start by finding what you already know that nobody has written down, then make it undeniable. Posting frequency is the last thing we discuss, not the first.

principles.title: One clear position beats five accurate descriptions.
principles.description: Most executives describe themselves in a way that is entirely true and completely unmemorable. A position is a deliberate narrowing: it costs you the audience you were never going to win, and buys you the one you can own.

principles.title: Your method is your moat.
principles.description: Anyone can copy your service list. Nobody can copy a named framework that carries your judgement inside it. Naming how you work converts you from a vendor with opinions into an institution with a system.

principles.title: Proof beats promise, and specificity beats proof.
principles.description: "We drive growth" is noise. "We took a $40M logistics business from 11 to 34 percent EBITDA in nineteen months" is a magnet. The work is usually not achieving results — it is retrieving the ones you already have and refusing to round them off.

principles.title: If it needs you in the room, it does not scale.
principles.description: Your authority should work while you sleep: an asset a stranger can encounter, evaluate and act on without you present. Everything we build is designed to be forwarded by someone else to someone you have never met.

blocks.heading: These five principles are the foundation. The method is what turns them into a plan.
blocks.subheading: Most people who read this far already know they have an authority gap. The useful question is which one, and what to do first.

blocks.heading: Four pillars, in order. Skipping one is why most personal branding fails.

pillars.name: Position
pillars.summary: Decide precisely who you are for and what you are willing to be wrong about.
pillars.detail: Output: a positioning statement, a named enemy, and three claims you can defend under pressure.

pillars.name: Proof
pillars.summary: Retrieve and quantify the evidence already sitting in your history.
pillars.detail: Output: an evidence library — numbers, case narratives, named outcomes, third-party endorsements.

pillars.name: Package
pillars.summary: Convert your judgement into a named method others can reference without you.
pillars.detail: Output: your framework, your keynote, your book thesis, your one-page point of view.

pillars.name: Platform
pillars.summary: Place the assets where your specific rooms already look.
pillars.detail: Output: a twelve-month distribution plan built around three channels, not eleven.

blocks.heading: I spent nine years making other people famous before I understood what it actually took.
blocks.excerpt:
I ran communications for a company whose founder was, by any technical measure, the best in his field. He lost a nine-figure acquisition to a competitor with a worse product and a better-known chief executive. I watched him read the announcement in a boardroom and say nothing.

That night I went through everything we had ever published about him. It was all accurate. None of it was memorable. We had spent four years describing a man instead of positioning one.

I have spent every year since then working out the difference — and it turns out the difference is a method, not a personality.

blocks.heading: The questions I get asked most

faqs.question: How is this different from executive coaching?
faqs.answer: Executive coaching generally works on how you show up: presence, communication, confidence under pressure. Authority advisory works on what exists outside the room — your position, your documented evidence, your named method, and where those assets are placed. Many clients do both, and several of my clients came to me while still working with a coach. The two are complementary rather than competing.

faqs.question: How long before anything visible happens?
faqs.answer: Positioning is usually settled within the first four to six weeks, and clients report the internal effect immediately: conversations get easier because the answer to "what do you do" stops being a paragraph. External signals — inbound enquiries, speaking invitations, press citations — typically begin between months three and five. Anyone promising external results in the first sixty days is selling exposure, not authority.

faqs.question: Do you write content for me?
faqs.answer: No, and this is deliberate. Ghostwritten thought leadership fails for a specific reason: the value is in your judgement, and judgement cannot be outsourced without becoming generic. I build the structure, extract the thinking through interviews, and edit hard. You supply the opinions. Most clients spend around two hours a week on this.

faqs.question: What does an engagement cost?
faqs.answer: Executive advisory engagements start at $45,000 for six months. The leadership team intensive is priced per engagement, typically between $28,000 and $60,000 depending on the size of the team. Keynotes start at $35,000 within North America. I only take on six advisory clients at a time, so availability rather than price is usually the binding constraint.

faqs.question: What happens on the strategy call?
faqs.answer: Thirty minutes, no presentation. I ask what you have built, who currently knows about it, and what specifically prompted you to look for help now. By the end you will have my honest read on whether you have an authority gap worth investing in, and if so which of the four pillars is weakest. If I do not think I am the right person, I will say so and usually suggest who is.
